- overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.test.ts

Context: this step's pass criteria require: "Gallery images never mix colours when a colour resolves — test with a fixture where the wrong-colour group has MORE images than the right one, and assert the right one wins. Make it fail first by reverting to 'most images' to prove the test actually catches it." The implementer already tried exactly ONE mutation — fully reverting to the old unscoped "most images wins" logic — and reports that breaks 2 tests. Your job is to falsify this a DIFFERENT way: pick mutations the implementer did NOT try, actually apply them (temporarily, directly in the real source file), run the real test suite, capture the real output, then immediately revert before trying the next one.

Do this exactly, one at a time, reverting between each:

**Mutation A — break ONLY the viewType axis.** Inside `selectColourScopedImages`, temporarily change `viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE` to a hardcoded wrong value, e.g. `viewType: 'large'`, leaving the `variationValues` colour-scoping logic completely untouched. Run `npm run test -- productListCardMapper` (or `npx vitest run overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.test.ts`) for real. Record exactly which test names fail and how many. Then run `git checkout -- overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts` and confirm via `git diff overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts` that it shows NO output (fully reverted) before moving on.

**Mutation B — break ONLY the colour axis.** Inside `selectColourScopedImages`, temporarily change the `variationValues` line so colour-scoping is always disabled regardless of `colour`, e.g. hardcode `variationValues: {}` unconditionally (delete the `colour ? {...} : {}` ternary), leaving `viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE` correct. Run the same test command for real. Record exactly which test names fail. Specifically check: does the test named something like "scopes to viewType: medium alone when no colour resolves, ignoring other viewTypes even when they have more images" still PASS under this mutation? (It should, because that fixture has no `representedProduct`/`variants` at all, so `colour` was already `undefined` and `variationValues` was already `{}` for that fixture — meaning this mutation changes nothing for that specific fixture.) If it does still pass, that means that particular test provides ZERO coverage against a colour-scoping regression — only the MULTI_COLOUR_HIT-based tests would catch this mutation. Confirm which specific tests DO fail. Then revert exactly as in Mutation A and confirm clean via `git diff`.

**Mutation C (your choice) — try to find a blind spot.** Think of one more realistic mutation neither the implementer nor Mutations A/B covered (e.g., reading `filteredGroups[1]` instead of `filteredGroups[0]`, or passing `hit.variationAttributes` instead of `hit.imageGroups` — anything plausible a future refactor could accidentally introduce) and repeat the same apply → test → record → revert cycle.

For every mutation, paste the REAL terminal output (pass/fail counts, failing test names) — not a paraphrase or summary. Conclude explicitly: are the viewType axis and the colour axis each independently covered by at least one test that fails ONLY when that specific axis breaks? Is there any mutation you tried that neither of the two "colour-isolation" tests (nor any other test in the file) catches — i.e., a real blind spot?

Critical safety rule: after EVERY mutation, you must revert with `git checkout -- overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts` before doing anything else. At the very end, run `git status` AND `git diff --stat` and paste both outputs to prove the working tree is clean (identical to whatever it was before you started — do not leave the file modified). If for any reason you cannot get back to a clean state, say so explicitly and paste the exact remaining diff — do not hide it or paper over it.

Keep your final report focused: one short paragraph per mutation (A, B, C) with real pass/fail evidence, then your conclusion, then the final git status/diff proof. Under ~600 words excluding pasted terminal output.

1	import type { ShopperSearchTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
2	import { getPriceData, filterImageGroups } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils';
3	import { productUrlBuilder } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url';
4	import type {
5	  ZimmProductCardBaseProps,
6	  ZimmProductCardPlpVariation,
7	  ZimmProductCardImage,
8	} from '../../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard';
9	import type { ZimmSizeChipValue } from '../../components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup';
10	
11	// This mapper is PLP-only by design, so it returns the narrowed shape directly rather than the
12	// full `ZimmProductCardProps` union — letting a caller pass the result straight to a
13	// PLP-typed component (like this page's own `ProductListCard`) with no re-narrowing needed.
14	type ProductListCardResult = ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardPlpVariation;
15	
16	/**
17	 * `c_productBadges` is a custom SFCC attribute (SFCC-225's own already-merged SCAPI hook) with no
18	 * typed field on the base SDK's `ProductSearchHit` — it only reaches this shape via that type's
19	 * own `{[key: string]: any}` index signature. Narrowed here to the one shape this mapper reads,
20	 * rather than trusting `any` at every call site.
21	 */
22	export type ProductListSearchHit = ShopperSearchTypes.ProductSearchHit & {
23	  c_productBadges?: Array<{ productBadge?: string }>;
24	};
25	
26	type RawImage = { alt?: string; disBaseLink?: string; link?: string };
27	
28	const toCardImage = (image: RawImage | undefined): ZimmProductCardImage | undefined => {
29	  const src = image?.disBaseLink ?? image?.link;
30	  if (!src) return undefined;
31	  return { src, alt: image?.alt ?? '' };
32	};
33	
34	/** The correctly-sized product image view the colour+viewType-scoped trio below all read — never
35	 *  serve an arbitrary-sized image at gallery/thumbnail size (AGENTS.md's image-sizing guidance).
36	 *  Matches `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s / `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s own identically-named,
37	 *  identically-valued constant. Named per conventions.md's no-magic-strings rule. */
38	const MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium';
39	
40	/**
41	 * The real, live SFCC `variationAttributes`/`variationValues` id for colour — confirmed directly
42	 * against a real 2-colour product (`ZWNEWPRD04`, colours BLK/TAN), each with its own separate
43	 * `imageGroups` entry tagged `variationAttributes: [{id: 'color', values: [{value: 'BLK'}]}]`.
44	 * Named per conventions.md's no-magic-strings rule. American spelling because this documents the
45	 * real, live SFCC attribute id (data, not a Zimmermann-authored identifier) — see
46	 * `resolveRepresentativeColour` below for the Australian-spelled function/variable naming this
47	 * constant feeds.
48	 */
49	const COLOR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'color';
50	
51	/**
52	 * Resolves the colour SFCC's own search index already chose to represent this hit — added
53	 * 2026-09-09 (plan addendum §7, step C1) to close a confirmed live defect: this mapper's gallery
54	 * used to be picked with no colour (or viewType) filter at all — "whichever image group has the
55	 * most images" — so a multi-colour product's gallery could show the wrong colour's photos.
56	 * Confirmed live against a real 2-colour product (`ZWNEWPRD04`, BLK/TAN): each colour has its own
57	 * separate, explicitly-tagged `imageGroups` entry, so the old "most images wins" heuristic could
58	 * (and did) pick the wrong one whenever the off-colour group happened to have more photos.
59	 *
60	 * `hit.representedProduct.id` is the specific variant SFCC's search index already picked to
61	 * represent this (typically master-level) hit; matching it against `hit.variants[]` by
62	 * `productId` finds that exact variant's own `variationValues.color` — deterministic and
63	 * server-decided, no guessing and no reliance on the untyped `c_color` custom attribute. There is
64	 * no colour selector on this card and none is being added here — this only teaches the mapper to
65	 * respect the colour SFCC already chose, not to let the shopper pick a different one.
66	 *
67	 * @returns `undefined` when there is no `representedProduct`, no `variants` array, or no variant
68	 *   whose `productId` matches it — callers scope to `viewType` alone in that case (see
69	 *   `selectColourScopedImages` below), never back to the old fully-unscoped "biggest group
70	 *   anywhere" pick.
71	 */
72	export const resolveRepresentativeColour = (hit: ProductListSearchHit): string | undefined => {
73	  const representedProductId = hit.representedProduct?.id;
74	  if (!representedProductId) return undefined;
75	
76	  const representativeVariant = hit.variants?.find((variant) => variant.productId === representedProductId);
77	  return representativeVariant?.variationValues?.[COLOR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID];
78	};
79	
80	/**
81	 * The colour+viewType-scoped image array `selectGalleryImages`, `hoverImage`, and
82	 * `primaryImageFallbacks` are all derived from — resolved via `resolveRepresentativeColour` so
83	 * all three read the same deterministic colour. Replaces the old viewType/colour-agnostic
84	 * "whichever group has the most images" pick entirely (plan addendum §7, step C1, 2026-09-09) —
85	 * when no colour resolves (single-colour product, or no `variants`/`representedProduct` match),
86	 * this still scopes to `viewType: 'medium'` alone and never falls back to that old fully-unscoped
87	 * behaviour.
88	 *
89	 * Only the first matching image group is read (`filteredGroups[0]`), matching
90	 * `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s / `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s own `selectPrimaryImage`
91	 * precedent for the same `filterImageGroups` call — a colour+viewType pair identifies at most one
92	 * real group in practice, so there is nothing to gain from reading past the first match.
93	 *
94	 * `hit.image` (the required `primaryImage` slot) is untouched by this and resolved exactly as
95	 * before by `selectProductListCard` — this array only ever supplies the gallery/hover-swap/
96	 * fallback candidates, never the primary image itself.
97	 */
98	const selectColourScopedImages = (hit: ProductListSearchHit): ZimmProductCardImage[] => {
99	  const colour = resolveRepresentativeColour(hit);
100	  const filteredGroups = filterImageGroups(hit.imageGroups ?? [], {
101	    viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
102	    variationValues: colour ? { [COLOR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID]: colour } : {},
103	  }) as ShopperSearchTypes.ImageGroup[];
104	
105	  const groupImages = filteredGroups[0]?.images ?? [];
106	  return groupImages.map(toCardImage).filter((img): img is ZimmProductCardImage => Boolean(img));
107	};
108	
109	/**
110	 * Picks this hit's gallery from the colour+viewType-scoped image array (see
111	 * `selectColourScopedImages` above) — rebuilt 2026-09-09 (plan addendum §7, step C1) to replace
112	 * the old viewType/colour-agnostic "biggest group anywhere" pick, a confirmed live defect (see
113	 * `selectColourScopedImages`'s own docblock). Returns `undefined` for 0 or 1 resulting images,
114	 * matching `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own "no gallery" contract for that case — this function
115	 * doesn't duplicate that check, it just never returns a 1-length array.
116	 */
117	export const selectGalleryImages = (hit: ProductListSearchHit): ZimmProductCardImage[] | undefined => {
118	  const images = selectColourScopedImages(hit);
119	  return images.length > 1 ? images : undefined;
120	};
121	
122	/**
123	 * Reads the "size" variation attribute (if this hit has one) into the shape
124	 * `ZimmSizeChipGroup` expects. `orderable` on each value already reflects real stock per that
125	 * specific size, so it maps directly to `isDisabled` with no extra lookup needed.
126	 */
127	export const selectSizeChipValues = (hit: ProductListSearchHit): ZimmSizeChipValue[] => {
128	  const sizeAttribute = hit.variationAttributes?.find((attr) => attr.id === 'size');
129	  return (sizeAttribute?.values ?? []).map((value) => ({
130	    value: value.value,
131	    label: value.name ?? value.value,
132	    isDisabled: value.orderable === false,
133	  }));
134	};
135	
136	/** What `resolveOrderableVariant` resolves a selected size chip value to — the real, orderable
137	 *  SKU for that specific size, not the master/represented-product id this hit otherwise defaults
138	 *  to. `price` is the variant's own (`ShopperSearchTypes.Variant`'s own field, confirmed real via
139	 *  a live product-detail check, 2026-09-08), which can genuinely differ from the hit's own flat
140	 *  `price` across sizes (e.g. plus sizes priced higher) — callers should prefer this over the
141	 *  hit's own price once a variant has been resolved. */
142	export type ResolvedVariant = {
143	  productId: string;
144	  price: number | undefined;
145	  orderable: boolean;
146	};
147	
148	/**
149	 * Resolves a selected size CHIP VALUE to its real orderable variant — added 2026-09-08 (Gap 3:
150	 * "size-aware Add to Bag" was previously cosmetic; selecting a chip never changed what got added
151	 * to the bag at all). Confirmed live against product `4673TS251`: `hit.variants` is real and
152	 * populated (`expand: [...,'variations']`, already requested by this page's own search call),
153	 * each entry carrying its own real `productId` (e.g. `4673TS251GVSCP0P`) keyed by
154	 * `variationValues.size` (e.g. `'0P'`) — exactly the lookup this function performs.
155	 *
156	 * Returns `null` when there is no matching variant at all (no `variants` array, or no entry
157	 * whose `variationValues.size` equals `sizeValue`) — callers are expected to fall back to this
158	 * hit's own default `representedProduct`/`productId` resolution in that case, the same default
159	 * that already existed before size-aware add-to-bag was ever selectable.
160	 */
161	export const resolveOrderableVariant = (hit: ProductListSearchHit, sizeValue: string): ResolvedVariant | null => {
162	  const variant = hit.variants?.find((candidate) => candidate.variationValues?.size === sizeValue);
163	  if (!variant) return null;
164	
165	  return {
166	    productId: variant.productId,
167	    price: variant.price,
168	    orderable: variant.orderable !== false,
169	  };
170	};
171	
172	/**
173	 * `getPriceData`'s own return shape (base SFCC, `product-utils.js:123-170`), narrowed to the
174	 * three fields this mapper reads — ported verbatim from `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s own
175	 * identically-named type, same reasoning: `@salesforce/retail-react-app` ships no types for this
176	 * subpath (falls through `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`'s catch-all ambient `any`), so this
177	 * documents an assumed shape rather than letting `any` propagate — the real correctness proof is
178	 * this file's own test comparing against a real `getPriceData` call, not this annotation alone.
179	 */
180	type SfccPriceData = {
181	  /** `findLowestPrice()`'s own `minPrice` — replaces the flat `hit.price` field this mapper used
182	   *  to read for `currentPrice` (2026-09-08: now sourced from the same call as `originalPrice`,
183	   *  closing the "two fields could disagree on a multi-variant hit" gap the old code risked). */
184	  currentPrice: number;
185	  /** The highest tiered price found — "was" price. `undefined` when the hit has no
186	   *  `tieredPrices` at all (there is then no maximum to compute). */
187	  listPrice: number | undefined;
188	  /** `currentPrice < listPrice` — always `false`, never `true`, when `listPrice` is `undefined`. */
189	  isOnSale: boolean;
190	};
191	
192	/**
193	 * Derives `currentPrice`/`originalPrice` from a single `getPriceData(hit)` call — ported verbatim
194	 * from `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s own `selectPriceFields` (see that file's own docblock
195	 * for why both fields must come from the one call rather than mixing a flat price field for one
196	 * and `getPriceData` for the other). No `opts` passed — the default `quantity: 1` is correct for
197	 * a single-unit card display. No hardcoded fallback currency — if either the price or the
198	 * currency is absent, formatting is skipped rather than guessed.
199	 *
200	 * **Closes 2026-09-08's confirmed gap**: this hit's own `perPricebook: true` + `expand: [...,
201	 * 'prices']` request (product-list/index.tsx) does carry real tiered pricing — checked directly
202	 * against a live on-sale product via the Shopper Products detail endpoint (same underlying
203	 * pricebook data; the search endpoint's own live response couldn't be intercepted directly, since
204	 * this page's initial data arrives via SSR with no separate client-side request to inspect) —
205	 * closing the honest "not checked against a live hit" caveat this file's own history carried.
206	 */
207	const selectPriceFields = (
208	  hit: ProductListSearchHit,
209	  formatPrice: (amount: number, currency: string) => string,
210	): Pick<ProductListCardResult, 'currentPrice' | 'originalPrice'> => {
211	  const priceData: SfccPriceData = getPriceData(hit);
212	
213	  const currentPrice =
214	    typeof priceData.currentPrice === 'number' && hit.currency
215	      ? formatPrice(priceData.currentPrice, hit.currency)
216	      : undefined;
217	
218	  // Only set when isOnSale is true -- a not-on-sale hit must not render a crossed-out price
219	  // identical to its current one.
220	  const originalPrice =
221	    priceData.isOnSale && typeof priceData.listPrice === 'number' && hit.currency
222	      ? formatPrice(priceData.listPrice, hit.currency)
223	      : undefined;
224	
225	  return { currentPrice, originalPrice };
226	};
227	
228	/**
229	 * Maps one real product-search hit to `ZimmProductCardProps` (`variation: 'plp'`) for this quick
230	 * test integration. `formatPrice` is passed in rather than built here — the page already owns an
231	 * `intl`-based formatter, and this stays a pure function with no `react-intl` dependency of its
232	 * own, the same split the page's existing wishlist-toast handlers already follow.
233	 *
234	 * Returns `null` when there's no usable name or primary image — mirrors `ZimmProductName`'s own
235	 * "no render without a name" contract, and `ZimmProductCardBaseProps.primaryImage`'s required-ness
236	 * (a card with neither has nothing to legitimately render).
237	 *
238	 * **`hoverImage`/`primaryImageFallbacks` added 2026-09-09 (plan addendum §7, step C1)** — both
239	 * read off the same colour+viewType-scoped array `images` is built from (see
240	 * `selectColourScopedImages`), never off `hit.image`. `hit.image` (`primaryImage` above) is
241	 * untouched by this addendum and still resolved exactly as before.
242	 */
243	export const selectProductListCard = (
244	  hit: ProductListSearchHit,
245	  formatPrice: (amount: number, currency: string) => string,
246	): ProductListCardResult | null => {
247	  const primaryImage = toCardImage(hit.image);
248	  if (!hit.productName || !primaryImage) return null;
249	
250	  const { currentPrice, originalPrice } = selectPriceFields(hit, formatPrice);
251	
252	  // hoverImage/primaryImageFallbacks are the second entry and the remainder of the same
253	  // colour+viewType-scoped array `images` (below) is built from — see
254	  // `selectColourScopedImages`'s own docblock. Computed via a second, independent call so
255	  // `selectGalleryImages` keeps its own single-argument, independently-testable public signature
256	  // rather than needing the array threaded in. `hit.image` (primaryImage above) is untouched by
257	  // this — it stays the sole source for primaryImage, exactly as before.
258	  const colourScopedImages = selectColourScopedImages(hit);
259	  const hoverImage = colourScopedImages[1];
260	  const primaryImageFallbacks = colourScopedImages.slice(2);
261	
262	  return {
263	    id: hit.productId,
264	    href: productUrlBuilder({ id: hit.productId }),
265	    name: hit.productName,
266	    headingLevel: 'h3',
267	    primaryImage,
268	    primaryImageFallbacks,
269	    hoverImage,
270	    images: selectGalleryImages(hit),
271	    currentPrice,
272	    originalPrice,
273	    isUnavailable: hit.orderable === false,
274	    // Single highest-priority badge — SFCC-225's own confirmed shape (see the organism's own
275	    // docblock, "Badge count" note): only one badge is ever shown, never a list.
276	    badge: hit.c_productBadges?.[0]?.productBadge,
277	    variation: 'plp',
278	    sizeChipValues: selectSizeChipValues(hit),
279	  };
280	};
